questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Mia joins two identical squares along one full side. What shape does she make?
questions.explanation: Two squares side by side make a longer shape with two long sides and two short sides. That is a rectangle.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Sam puts 4 identical square tiles in a row. Each tile has sides of 3 cm. How many centimetres long is the row?
questions.explanation: The row is 4 tiles long and each tile is 3 cm. 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A flat hexagon has 6 equal sides. It is made from identical triangles that all meet in the middle. How many triangles are there?
questions.explanation: Each side of the hexagon is the bottom of one triangle. There are 6 sides, so there are 6 triangles.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Ben draws a house by putting a triangle on top of a square. He traces around the outside of the whole shape. How many straight sides does the outline have?
questions.explanation: The triangle sits on the top side of the square, so that side is hidden. The square leaves 3 sides and the triangle adds 2. 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A map grid names each square with its column letter first, then its row number. The oval is in column D and row 2. What is its grid reference?
questions.explanation: The letter comes first and the number comes second. Column D and row 2 is D2.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Lena leaves her campsite and walks 2 km west. Then she walks 2 km north. In which direction is the campsite from where she is now?
questions.explanation: She went west and then north. To get back she must go the opposite ways: east and south. That is south-east.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: On a school map, the flagpole is at C2. The canteen is at C6. They are in the same column. How many squares apart are they?
questions.explanation: Count up from row 2 to row 6: 3, 4, 5, 6. That is 4 squares. Or work out 6 − 2 = 4.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Ali starts at the library at A1 on a map grid. Letters go up to the right, and numbers go up as you move up the map. He moves 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. Where does he finish?
questions.explanation: Moving right 3 squares changes the letter from A to D. Moving up 2 squares changes the number from 1 to 3. He finishes at D3.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square can be folded in half up and down, across, and along both corners. That makes 4 lines.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Which capital letter has no line of symmetry?
questions.explanation: If you fold F in half either way, the two sides do not match. H, O and X all fold to match.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Which shape looks the same after a half turn, but has no line of symmetry?
questions.explanation: A slanted parallelogram matches itself after a half turn. It cannot be folded to match. The triangle and kite fold to match but do not match after a half turn. A square does both.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry.
questions.explanation: You can fold it in half along its length or across its width. The diagonals do not work, so there are 2 lines.
